steps.title: Reactivity series
steps.body: A list of metals arranged in order of their reactivity, from most reactive to least reactive. The more reactive a metal, the more easily it loses electrons to form positive ions.

steps.title: Displacement reaction
steps.body: A reaction in which a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.

steps.title: Oxidation
steps.body: A reaction in which a substance gains oxygen or loses electrons (OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons).

steps.title: Reduction
steps.body: A reaction in which a substance loses oxygen or gains electrons (Reduction Is Gain of electrons).

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series react with acids to produce a salt and hydrogen gas. Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + H₂(g) Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g) Worked Example 2: Reaction of iron with acid Write the equation for iron reacting with hydrochloric acid. Iron is Fe, forms Fe²⁺ ions. Hydrochloric acid is HCl. Word: iron + hydrochloric acid → iron(II) chloride + hydrogen Symbol: Fe(s) + 2HCl(aq) → FeCl₂(aq) + H₂(g)

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Foundation List the following metals in order of reactivity (most reactive first): copper, potassium, iron, zinc, sodium. | Foundation Write the word equation for calcium reacting with cold water. | Higher Will magnesium displace copper from copper(II) sulfate solution? Write the balanced symbol equation if a reaction occurs.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Potassium, sodium, zinc, iron, copper (from most to least reactive) | Calcium + water → calcium hydroxide + hydrogen | Yes — magnesium is more reactive than copper, so displacement occurs. Mg(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → MgSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the reactivity series order — use a mnemonic that works for you Carbon is not a metal but you must know its position — it determines which extraction method is used In displacement questions, always check the reactivity series first before predicting if a reaction will occur State symbols matter: (aq) for dissolved salts, (s) for solid metals, (g) for gases When asked about oxidation and reduction, state whether you are referring to oxygen or electrons Observations in displacement reactions: the solution changes colour and a solid appears
